title: Little Office of S. Philip Neri, Founder of the Congregation of the Oratory
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Te Philippe quam amavit Dei providentia! Quam te Numen exornavit Singulari gratia! A juventae pietatis, Mirae jam sanctitatis Dederas specimina.
blocks.english: How God’s providence loved thee, Philip! How God adorned thee with singular grace! From youth thou hadst already given signs of devotion and wondrous holiness.

blocks.source: Ant. Philippus piis, honestisque parentibus Florentiae natus, ab ipsa ineunte aetate non obscura dedit futurae sanctitatis indicia.
blocks.english: Ant. Philip, born at Florence of devout and honourable parents, from his earliest age gave clear indications of his future holiness.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Philippe Neri,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Philip Neri,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Oclementissime Deus, qui dilectum famulum tuum Philippum Nerium jam tenera in aetate multis sanctitatis tuae signis decorasti: oramus te igitur per insignia sancti tui merita, ut nos ad illum virtutis tramitem dirigere digneris, qui nos ad te, tanquam ad finem, unicamque animae nostrae metam perducat. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum etc. Amen.
blocks.english: O most merciful God, who didst adorn Thy beloved servant Philip Neri even in tender age with many signs of Thy holiness, we therefore pray through the outstanding merits of Thy saint that Thou mayest deign to guide us upon that path of virtue which leads us to Thee as our end and the sole goal of our soul. Through Jesus Christ, Thy Son, our Lord, who with Thee, etc. Amen.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Iter Romam subiit, Charam linquens patriam, Raram ubi ostendit Indolis praestantiam, Totum Christo te sacrando, Libertatem resignando, Vitam et substantiam.
blocks.english: He journeyed to Rome, leaving his beloved homeland, where he showed rare excellence of character, consecrating himself wholly to Christ and surrendering freedom, life, and possessions.

blocks.source: Ant. Ampla patrii haereditate dimissa Romam se contulit, ubi Philosophiae et Sacris Literis eruditus, atque sacerdos ex ordinatione factus, totum se Christo dicavit.
blocks.english: Ant. Giving up his ample paternal inheritance, he went to Rome, where, instructed in philosophy and sacred letters and ordained a priest, he dedicated himself wholly to Christ.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Philippe Neri,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Philip Neri,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Obenignissime Deus, qui dilectum famulum tuum Philippum Nerium ad singularem tui notitiam eveheti; adeo, ut sanctissimae tuae totum sese voluntati transcriberit: dignare, o Deus, et nos per sancti tui merita, ad talem tui notitiam perducere, ut nihil, quam tui soli fovere cupiamus. Per Dominum nostrum etc.
blocks.english: O most gracious God, who didst raise Thy beloved servant Philip Neri to a singular knowledge of Thee, so that he committed himself wholly to Thy most holy will, deign, O God, through the merits of Thy saint, to lead us also to such knowledge of Thee that we may desire to cherish nothing but Thee alone. Through our Lord, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints the malformed verbs “eveheti” and “transcriberit.” The English provisionally follows the petition’s context of knowledge and dedication; the Latin remains.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Totum Dei dum amore Pectus suum aestuat, Tota proximi ardore Mensque incaluerat,
blocks.english: While his whole breast burns with love of God and his whole mind had grown warm with ardour for his neighbour,

blocks.source: Dic! quot fervor animarum Iste fontes lachrymarum Tibi non extorserat?
blocks.english: Tell me, how many fountains of tears did this zeal for souls draw forth from thee!

blocks.source: Ant. Tanto Cor ejus aestuabat amore, ut cum inter fines suos contineri non posset, confractis duabus costis, Dominus illud mirabiliter ampliaverit.
blocks.english: Ant. His heart burned with such love that, unable to remain within its bounds, the Lord wonderfully enlarged it, breaking two ribs.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Philippe Neri,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Philip Neri,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Oamantissime Deus, qui famulum tuum Philippum Nerium tanto tui amoris incendio inflammasti, ut saepius igneae ex oculis erumperent scintillae viderentur, tantoque hic etiam proximi ardore flagraret, ut persaepe copiosissimos lachrymarum imbres effunderet: rogamus te igitur, o fons veri amoris, per merita famuli tui, ut tantum tui proximique amorem cordibus nostris infundas, quo nihil aliud quam te, et proximum diligere cogitemus. Per Dominum nostrum etc.
blocks.english: O most loving God, who didst inflame Thy servant Philip Neri with so great a fire of Thy love that fiery sparks often seemed to burst from his eyes, and who burned also with such ardour for his neighbour that he often poured forth most abundant showers of tears, we therefore beseech Thee, fountain of true love, through the merits of Thy servant, to pour such love of Thee and our neighbour into our hearts that we may think of nothing but loving Thee and our neighbour. Through our Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Tu parabas afflictorum Cordibus solatia, Indurata peccatorum Molliens praecordia; Quotquot ad te proflugebant, Opem inter pericula Curas et pericula.
blocks.english: Thou didst prepare consolations for the hearts of the afflicted, softening the hardened hearts of sinners; all who fled to thee sought help amid dangers, cares, and perils.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF repeats dangers with incomplete syntax in the closing lines. The English provisionally understands seeking help amid cares and dangers; the Latin remains.

blocks.source: Ant. Egenos et pauperes omni charitatis officio prosequebatur, absentibus inferendum apparatu, ipsis de periculantibus open cultu.
blocks.english: Ant. He attended the needy and poor with every service of charity. [The remaining printed clause, “absentibus inferendum apparatu, ipsis de periculantibus open cultu,” is unintelligible.]
blocks.editorialNote: The printed clause after the first statement of charity is unintelligible and explicitly marked untranslated in English. It requires source resolution.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Philippe Neri,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Philip Neri,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Misericordissime Domine, qui sanctum Philippum Nerium tantis gratiarum cumulasti divitiis, ut omnes quibuscunque angustiarum afflictionibus pressi, solamen apud ipsum quaerentes, securissime illud invenerint: da igitur, o Pater misericordiarum, ut beati hujus famuli tui meritis, et nos a gravioribus animi anxietatibus atque periculis liberemur. Per Dominum etc.
blocks.english: Most merciful Lord, who didst heap upon Saint Philip Neri such riches of grace that all who, oppressed by any distressing afflictions, sought consolation with him most surely found it, grant therefore, O Father of mercies, that through the merits of this blessed servant we too may be freed from graver anxieties and dangers of the soul. Through the Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Illium Virginitatis Custodivit sedulo, Ut in flore puritatis Viveret perpetuo, Tela Cypridis vicit, Et illius vim fregit Forti precum gladio.
blocks.english: He diligently guarded the lily of virginity, that he might live for ever in the flower of purity. He conquered the darts of Cypris and broke her power with the mighty sword of prayer.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Illium Virginitatis” is provisionally understood as “Lilium,” lily; the Latin remains. Cypris, the classical name for Venus, is retained as the poem’s imagery.

blocks.source: Ant. Virginitatem perpetuo illibatam servavit id affectus, ut eos, qui puritatem colerent, ex odore, qui vero secus, ex foetore dignosceret.
blocks.english: Ant. He preserved his virginity perpetually undefiled, being so endowed that he distinguished those who cherished purity by fragrance, and those who did otherwise by a foul smell.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Philippe Neri,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Philip Neri,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Opurissime Domine, et tenerime Virginis castitatis amator, qui sanctum Philippum Nerium speciali hoc gratiae dono exornasti, quod ejusdem corpus tam amabilem castitatis odorem reddidit, ut omnes, qui illud adstarent, mirabiliter suavi recrearet: oramus te igitur, per insignem hanc famuli tui castimoniam, ut nos ad candidam puritatis lilium donare digneris, et aliquando digni habeamur, te purissimum et divinissimum Sponsum a facie ad faciem intueri. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum etc.
blocks.english: O most pure Lord and tenderest lover of virginal chastity, who didst adorn Saint Philip Neri with this special gift of grace, that his body gave forth so lovely a fragrance of chastity that it refreshed all who stood near it with wondrous sweetness, we therefore pray through this outstanding purity of Thy servant that Thou mayest deign to grant us the white lily of purity, and that one day we may be found worthy to behold Thee, most pure and divine Bridegroom, face to face. Through Jesus our Lord, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF has irregular endings and syntax, including “ad candidam puritatis lilium donare.” The English provisionally understands the petition for purity; the Latin remains.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Diu postquam praeluxit Mira patientia, Et virtutum coluit Ferrea constantia, Qua te per sanctam mortem Christus, o beatam sortem, Vocat ad convivia.
blocks.english: After long shining with wondrous patience and cultivating virtues with iron steadfastness, Christ, through holy death, calls thee to His banquet: O blessed lot!
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF changes grammatical person and has the irregular “Et virtutum coluit.” The English provisionally renders a narrative of steadfast virtue and the call to heaven; the Latin remains.

blocks.source: Ant. Octava Calendas Junias, in quem diem incidebat festum Corporis Christi, sacroque maxima Spiritus exultatione peracto, mediam noctem octogenarius obdormivit in Domino.
blocks.english: Ant. On the eighth day before the Kalends of June, upon which fell the feast of Corpus Christi, having celebrated the sacred rite with the greatest joy of spirit, at midnight, aged eighty, he fell asleep in the Lord.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Philippe Neri,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Philip Neri,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Opatientissime Domine, et virtutis praemiator, qui miram beati famuli tui Philippi Neri in adversis patientiam, et eximiam virtutis constantiam aeterni in coelo gloria remunerasti: quaesumus Domine, ut nos quoque, per gloriosa sancti tui suffragia, fortes in rebus omnibus adversis patientiam, et heroicam in virtutis tramite constantiam usque ad vitae nostrae exitum mereamur servare. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum etc.
blocks.english: O most patient Lord and rewarder of virtue, who didst reward in heaven’s eternal glory the wondrous patience in adversity and outstanding steadfastness in virtue of Thy blessed servant Philip Neri, we beseech Thee, O Lord, that through the glorious prayers of Thy saint we too may be found worthy to preserve brave patience in all adversities and heroic steadfastness upon the path of virtue until the end of our life. Through Jesus our Lord, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF has irregular case endings in the eternal-glory and patience clauses. The English provisionally renders the intelligible petition; the Latin remains.

blocks.source: ℣. Convertere nos Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: O Philippe coeli lumen, Clericorum gloria, Per quem maxima jam Numen Exhibet miracula; Esto nobis semper pronus, Dux fidelis et patronus, Quavis in miseria.
blocks.english: O Philip, light of heaven and glory of the clergy, through whom God now displays the greatest miracles, be always favourable to us, a faithful guide and patron in every misery.

blocks.source: Ant. Innumeros pene filios Christo peperit, aegrotos plurimos, mortique proximos restituit sanitati, et mortuorum revocavit ad vitam.
blocks.english: Ant. He brought forth almost innumerable children for Christ, restored very many sick persons and those near death to health, and recalled the dead to life.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Philippe Neri,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Philip Neri,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Opatientissime Domine, qui insignem sancti Philippi Nerii sanctitatem plurimis illustrasti miraculis, adeo, ut gloriosum illius nomen omnium extollatur linguis, ac celebretur encomiis: oramus te igitur, ut nos beati hujus famuli tui meritorum facere digneris participes. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum etc.
blocks.english: O most patient Lord, who didst illuminate the outstanding holiness of Saint Philip Neri with very many miracles, so that his glorious name is exalted by every tongue and celebrated with praises, we therefore pray that Thou mayest deign to make us sharers in the merits of this blessed servant of Thine. Through Jesus Christ our Lord, etc.

blocks.source: Hasce supplices, beate, Preces tibi suscipe, Sint te hic dedicatae Intimo ex pectore: Adsis nobis o patrone, Nunc et mortis in agone Nos Philippe protege.
blocks.english: O blessed one, receive these humble prayers, dedicated to thee from the depths of our heart. Be with us, O patron, now and in death’s struggle; protect us, Philip.

blocks.source: Ant. Verbo Dei, sacramentorum frequentia, orationis assiduitate, aliisque pietatis operibus omnes cupiens enutriri, Oratorii instituit congregationem.
blocks.english: Ant. Desiring all to be nourished by the word of God, frequent reception of the sacraments, assiduous prayer, and other works of devotion, he founded the Congregation of the Oratory.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Philippe Neri,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Philip Neri,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus, Deus, qui beatum Philippum confessorem tuum sanctorum gloria sublimasti: concede, propitius, ut ejus solemnitate laetamur, ejus virtutem prosequamur exemplis. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum etc.
blocks.english: Let us pray. O God, who didst raise Blessed Philip Thy confessor to the glory of the saints, mercifully grant that, as we rejoice in his solemnity, we may pursue his virtue by following his examples. Through Jesus Christ our Lord, etc.

editorialNotes.text: English prepared after visual comparison with PDF pages 586–589. The seven printed hours and Commendation retain their distinct collects and antiphons; no shared collect or Lauds is invented. The source’s narrative and classical imagery are preserved. One unintelligible antiphon clause is explicitly untranslated; other defective grammar is provisional and marked inline.
